newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro bourse 1996 turnover nearly doubles.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro bourse 1996 turnover nearly doubles.

text.p: The Montenegro Stock Exchange said on Tuesday its 1996 turnover will exceed 600 million dinars ($117 million). In 1995 turnover was 322.2 million dinars.

Some analysts said the rise in turnover resulted from changes in the dinar exchange rate. Until November 1995, the dinar was fixed to the German mark at par. After a 70 percent devaluation, its rate was changed to 3.3.

Short-term securities accounted for almost 59 percent of the total, with the remainder generated in the so-called giro-money market segment, where banks trade their surplus liquidity, the head of the Montenegro bourse told Reuters.
"This was a year of slight progress in attempting to create a real market activity. But a high volume of over-the-counter deals still remains a big problem," Milasin Borovic said.
Borovic called on all brokerages to conduct at least 51 percent of their activity on the official market.
"This is a matter of transparency, prices (of the security) and matching supply and demand," he said.
Activity on the Montenegro bourse is expected to grow in 1997 along with further privatisation.
"We expect at least 10 local companies to list shares on the bourse in 1997. And we will form the official list A for the top companies, while the rest will be placed on list B," Borovic said.
Head of the Podgorica-based Montenegro bourse saw the Yugoslav financial market remaining in its first stage until privatisation progresses.
"Without a capital market there will be no substantial development of the financial market either," he added.
However, some analysts feared the current political instability in Serbia could affect privatisation in Montenegro and frighten off foreign investors.
